notes: Written by `specify init` and its subcommands, as the tests of the integrations list them (https://github.com/github/spec-kit/blob/c6a4c18f1d01a8bec241c618eb6dfea952508744/tests/integrations/test_integration_base_skills.py). The managed .specify/.gitignore leaves "everything else under `.specify/` (constitution, templates, scripts, extension config) shareable". These files anchor the Spec Kit rows. Before version 0.0.22 the scripts/ and templates/ folders were at the project root (https://github.com/github/spec-kit/blob/v0.0.21/templates/plan-template.md).

"Persist the resolved path to `.specify/feature.json`" (https://github.com/github/spec-kit/blob/main/templates/commands/specify.md) (specify.md L99); gitignored by the managed .specify/.gitignore since v0.16.1 (2026-08-07), committed in many files before that (code search).

Spec Kit names a place for a roadmap of an epic, "For a feature-scoped epic: `specs/<epic-slug>/roadmap.md`." and "For a larger, cross-cutting epic: a top-level `ROADMAP.md`.", but writes none: "The roadmap is an ordinary Markdown file you author and keep under version control — there is no special tooling behind it." Without a name or a format of Spec Kit's own, such a roadmap cannot be told from the roadmaps that projects write without Spec Kit.

ralph-speckit, a plugin of smart-ralph, writes .specify/specs/ with numbered feature folders, "001-feature-name/", which rows count. Spec Kit itself names no .specify/specs/: a feature's "default location is under `specs/` in that project" (https://github.com/github/spec-kit/blob/main/docs/overview/core.md). A folder there without the number follows neither.

README L29-30: "OpenAI Codex, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot … Cursor Agent … Gemini CLI"; L398: "SpecDD specs use the `.sdd` extension." The extension is also StarOffice Draw/Impress's: the .sdd files in the sample are all such documents or binary test data (alfresco/alfresco-community-repo, apache/tika, richardlehane/siegfried). A text check would be needed; specs colocated with code are closer to rules than to plans.

Kiro is outside the six tools. It writes one folder per spec into `.kiro/specs/`: "you might organize your specs like this: … .kiro/specs/ ├── user-authentication/", and "Every spec generates three key files that form the foundation of your specification: requirements.md (or bugfix.md)" (https://kiro.dev/docs/specs/). Its steering is configuration: "Workspace steering files reside in your project root folder under .kiro/steering/" (https://kiro.dev/docs/steering/). Kiro writes a `.config.kiro` beside the documents, as in the evidence, and no `spec.json`, which separates its specs from those of cc-sdd.

"The plan file lives outside your repository"; "Plans are stored in ~/.devin/plans/ and are available in the @mentions menu". The Wayback Machine capture of 2026-05-29 (https://web.archive.org/web/20260529144606/https://docs.windsurf.com/windsurf/cascade/modes) is the last capture that names the earlier directory: "Plans are stored in your ~/.windsurf/plans directory and are available in the @mentions menu."

The memory bank of Cline: "memory-bank/ ├── projectbrief.md … productContext.md … activeContext.md … systemPatterns.md … techContext.md … progress.md". The /deep-planning command writes its plan with no stated folder: "Plan Creation - Generates implementation_plan.md with detailed specifications" (https://docs.cline.bot/core-workflows/using-commands). The memory bank "works with any AI that can read docs", and the page names none of the six tools. cursor-memory-bank, which names Cursor, has its own row anchored by tasks.md, creative/ or reflection/.
The rules of cursor-memory-bank name "Style Guide File: `memory-bank/style-guide.md`" among the core files. A style guide states conventions for the code rather than the work to do, as a rule does.

Kilo Code is outside the six tools. The plan agent has "restricted file editing (plan files in `.kilo/plans/` only)". The memory bank is in one of two folders: "Examine the contents in .kilo/rules/memory-bank/ (or the legacy .kilocode/rules/memory-bank/ )" (https://kilo.ai/docs/advanced-usage/memory-bank).
Architect mode has "restricted edit (markdown files only)" but no documented plan path.
Trae is an IDE outside the six tools. Of the October collection, only VisActor/VChart has `.trae/documents/`, and no vendor page that names the folder was found.
Seen in the sample only; no vendor page read.
Junie is outside the five; .junie/ holds its guidelines and commands (configuration). Seen in the sample; no Junie plan layout found.

GSD Pi "is a local-first coding agent for planning, implementing, verifying, and tracking project work from the command line", a tool outside the five that uses others only as model providers: "external CLI providers such as Claude Code and Cursor Agent". A team can commit its .gsd/: "If your team commits the `.gsd/` markdown (a real `.gsd/` directory with tracked files)" (https://github.com/open-gsd/gsd-pi/blob/main/docs/user-docs/working-in-teams.md). The GSD port for Copilot uses .gsd/ too, and its rows count a file beside the port's prompt files.
The settings of Get Shit Done: "├── config.json # Workflow configuration".
The research module's cache: "`.planning/research/.cache` for project-local web/synthesis results".

Indexes that the tool writes: the quick task archive "(re)writes that archive directory's `README.md` (an index built by scanning the archive directory" and "| `.planning/spikes/MANIFEST.md` | Index of all spikes with verdicts |" (https://github.com/open-gsd/gsd-core/blob/next/docs/features/spike-command.md).

Logs, reviews and reports of a phase or a project that no row counts yet, such as "**Produces:** `{phase}-CONTEXT.md`, `{phase}-DISCUSSION-LOG.md` (audit trail)", "**Produces:** `{phase}-REVIEW.md` with severity-classified findings; `{phase}-REVIEW-FIX.md` when `--fix` is used" and "**Produces:** `{phase}-SECURITY.md` with threat verification results". Whether an audit trail, a code review or a security audit is a planning document is open; the rows count the specs, plans, research, verification and acceptance results of a phase.

The record of what each repository released for a milestone, which milestone completion archives as JSON: "On success the map is written to `.planning/milestones/<version>-RELEASE-MAP.json`, a `**Release mapping:**` table is added to the MILESTONES.md entry". A milestone of a workstream keeps it in the workstream's folder: "`milestone complete --ws` archives into the workstream, not root ... releaseMapFile = releaseMapArchivePath(archiveDir, version);" (https://github.com/open-gsd/gsd-core/blob/d37ff11b47258b560f0cf8f1132b42ecd90e0c79/src/milestone.cts). MILESTONES.md, which shows the map as a table, counts.

The broken-windows ledger of Get Shit Done, which `/gsd-ship` reads when `workflow.windows_enforce` is set: it "blocks while `.planning/WINDOWS.md` reports any `open` entry." and "The ledger accumulates stubs, TODOs, skipped tests, unrun verifies, and unmet truths across phases." It records defects that the tool tracks across phases, not work that a plan describes.

"The App Prototyping agent generates an app blueprint based on your prompt, returning a proposed app name, required features, and style guidelines." The page states no file or folder for the blueprint, and Firebase Studio is not one of the six tools.
"* **Default**: unset, so Claude Code uses `~/.claude/plans`". The repository receives plans only where plansDirectory names a project directory (candidate row).

"Task lists written by the task tools, one directory per list" under ~/.claude/tasks/. Ultraplan: "Anthropic has removed the Ultraplan research preview." (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ultraplan), and the changelog of version 2.1.222: "Removed ultraplan feature" (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).
A prompt example, not a feature: "Interview me until you could write the spec, then write it to SPEC.md."

"Plans are saved by default in your home directory." Cursor's staff on the forum (https://forum.cursor.com/t/option-to-save-plans-in-project-level-cursor-directory/152291): "there isn’t a setting right now to always create plans in the project automatically".

Cursor stores the plans that it saves "to store plans in .cursor/plans/ ." with its own opening. A file there without it is a file that a person wrote, such as forcedotcom/salesforcedx-vscode's e2e-plan.md beside a plan of Cursor, and the folder's name alone does not tell such files from Cursor's plans.

Plan mode writes no file: "You must not perform **mutating** actions.", and "Not allowed (mutating, plan-executing)" lists "Editing or writing files". The plan is a `<proposed_plan>` block "so the client can render it specially", and `update_plan` only sends `EventMsg::PlanUpdate` (https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/plan.rs). The plan system skill of OpenAI's skills catalog saved plans in `$CODEX_HOME/plans` only: "Never write to the repo; only read files to understand context." (https://github.com/openai/skills/blob/5a9bb4cbe6d79d44aa619c70edbfa1654358f69c/skills/.system/plan/SKILL.md). The create-plan skill that replaced it writes nothing: "Throughout the entire workflow, operate in read-only mode. Do not write or update files." (https://github.com/openai/skills/blob/2a1cce6e760886d6cbd6d008708b60c1325d59cb/skills/.experimental/create-plan/SKILL.md).

The archived recipe names one path: "use an ExecPlan (as described in .agent/PLANS.md)". PLANS.md holds the rules for writing plans, which config_path_patterns.csv already collects (collect_only); no source names where the ExecPlans go ("Note that this is an arbitrary term, Codex has not been trained on it."). The count is of .agent(s)/plans/ folders, a user convention.

The layout of one internal product in OpenAI's post on harness engineering, which returns HTTP 403 to the documentation watch and is quoted from its capture of 2026-10-22 (https://web.archive.org/web/20261022025626/https://openai.com/index/harness-engineering/): "In-repository knowledge store layout."; the post warns: "This behavior depends heavily on the specific structure and tooling of this repository and should not be assumed to generalize". No Codex page or source names these folders, and the ExecPlans recipe names no place for the plans.
"writing a PLAN.md file that is committed to the codebase"; no location.

"The plan is stored in session memory at `/memories/session/plan.md`, not as a project file." Open in Editor makes an editable copy: "create an untitled copy of the plan, which you can save in your project." The copy is "#createFile the plan as is into an untitled file (`untitled:plan-${camelCaseName}.prompt.md` without frontmatter) for further refinement." (https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/113947563a3837013dbff0095e2bf29880b5d354/extensions/copilot/src/extension/agents/vscode-node/planAgentProvider.ts), saved wherever the user chooses and named as the prompt files of the evidence are.
Plan mode: "* Saves the plan to `plan.md` in your session folder."; session storage location: "~/.copilot/session-state/{session-id}/".
Copilot cloud agent plans in the session: "propose a plan before making changes." and "Review the plan and iterate with Copilot until it matches your intent." The page names no file.

No GitHub page names a PRD that Spark writes, and the template that a Spark app starts from contains `spark.meta.json` and no PRD.md. Spark is retired: "GitHub Spark was deprecated on August 31, 2026." A root PRD.md without Spark's files is a name that projects choose for their own requirements, as in the evidence, and no repository of the October collection has Spark's files.

Antigravity keeps its plans, task lists and walkthroughs in "the application's local app data directory `~/.gemini/antigravity/`", and no page documents a workspace location. Bare implementation_plan.md and walkthrough.md in repositories are other documents, except cerfacs-globc/icclim, which copied brain/<uuid>/ folders into doc/source/archive/.
By default, the plans "are stored in a managed temporary directory outside your project".

Jules's plan is an API activity (planGenerated, planApproved); Gemini Code Assist "might show a high-level plan for your approval" (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/docs/codeassist/agent-mode). Jules is not one of the six tools.

Traycer is "an open-source desktop app for running Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other AI coding agents in parallel" (https://docs.traycer.ai/). The documents of a task live in the app, and a host keeps a copy outside the repository. The copies "sync with the Task, so collaborators can open the published deliverables without sharing your repository folder." and "A host keeps its copy current only while the Task is open there or one of its agents is working in it.", in "`~/.traycer/epics/<task-id>/artifacts/`".

gstack "turns Claude Code (and other coding agents) into a virtual engineering team" (https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/blob/main/README.md). Office hours write design documents to "{gstack_state_root}/projects/{repo_slug}/*-design-*.md", outside the repository. gstack keeps "config, analytics, sessions, projects" under one directory, "the state root. By default that is `~/.gstack`." (https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/blob/main/docs/state-root.md). The state root is a relative .gstack only as the "Last resort when there is no home directory at all (some containers)." Inside a git repository, the agent also writes a copy into docs/designs/, which has a row of its own.

gstack keeps two root files that other projects name the same way. Its design consultation "builds your design system from scratch, researches what's out there, proposes creative risks, and writes `DESIGN.md`", and `/ship` "owns TODOS, release metadata, generation and publication" (https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/blob/main/docs/why-gstack.md); office hours "Read `CLAUDE.md`, `TODOS.md` (if they exist)." (https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/blob/main/office-hours/SKILL.md). The design consultation skill writes the file: "Phase 6 targets DESIGN.md." The October collection has a root DESIGN.md in many repositories and a root TODOS.md in a few, among them the evidence, which gstack did not write.

gstack's /spec writes a spec that is "filed as a GitHub issue, archived locally, and optionally piped to a spawned agent." The README names the "archive to `$GSTACK_STATE_ROOT/projects/$SLUG/specs/`" (https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/blob/main/README.md), which is outside the repository, under "the state root. By default that is `~/.gstack`." (https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/blob/main/docs/state-root.md). The state root is a relative .gstack only as the "Last resort when there is no home directory at all (some containers)."

Plannotator is a review interface for plans: "Install Plannotator, annotate plans and documents, review code changes, and return feedback to your coding agent.", for agents such as "Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode" (https://docs.plannotator.ai/llms.txt). What it writes stays in its data directory: "Configuration, session records, saved plans, document history, drafts, and Guided Reviews Under the active Plannotator data directory. This is normally `~/.plannotator`."

Memex connects "any MCP-compatible AI coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, or a custom agent)" to its server, which keeps the specs, decisions, acceptance criteria and tasks: "It provides a shared graph that both humans and AI coding agents read from and write to", and "Every Spec and every decision is vector indexed in the Postgres database". Its MCP tool `get` returns a spec as Markdown: "Read by canonical ref. view: content (default), tests (AC digest), export (markdown)".

layout: ~/.promptx/, or .promptx/ beside the docker-compose.yml of a Docker setup
notes: PromptX adds roles to "Claude, Cursor and other AI applications" (https://github.com/Deepractice/PromptX/blob/main/README.md). Its data folder holds roles, memory and configuration: "PromptX data is stored in `./.promptx` directory next to `docker-compose.yml` by default." and "This includes: - User roles - Memory data - Configuration files". The README mounts `~/.promptx` instead. None of these files is a spec, plan or task list.

Since July 2026 the outputs of the PRP skills are "stored outside the repository in a per-project directory:", with prds/, plans/, reports/ and reviews/, and "Set `PRP_HOME` to override the default `~/.prp` root."

visual-companion.md at version 5.0.0 (https://github.com/obra/superpowers/blob/v5.0.0/skills/brainstorming/visual-companion.md): "Remind the user to add `.superpowers/` to `.gitignore` if it's not already there."; subagent-driven-development SKILL.md calls .superpowers/sdd/ the plan's "git-ignored directory". Task briefs and reports of a running plan, not the plan.

layout: openspec/config.yaml; openspec/AGENTS.md, openspec/README.md (0.x); openspec/schemas/; .openspec-store/; root AGENTS.md block
notes: Configuration of OpenSpec. config.yaml holds "project settings and context for the AI" and anchors the layout. OpenSpec before 1.0 wrote its instructions into openspec/AGENTS.md, which the migration guide (https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec/blob/main/docs/migration-guide.md) lists as "Obsolete workflow trigger", and version 0.1.0 into openspec/README.md (https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec/blob/v0.1.0/src/core/templates/readme-template.ts): "This document provides instructions for AI coding assistants on how to use OpenSpec conventions for spec-driven development." A project's schemas customize the workflow (https://openspec.dev/docs/customize-schemas): "Your project: openspec/schemas/, committed with the repo so your whole team gets it." A store keeps its metadata in .openspec-store/store.yaml (https://openspec.dev/docs/cli): "With .openspec-store/store.yaml present, register reuses the recorded id." The OpenSpec block of the root AGENTS.md is part of a context file, which the migration guide cleans: "Only the OpenSpec marker blocks are removed; everything you wrote stays."

Conductor's setup copies style guides that the agent follows: "Select and copy appropriate style guides from assets/code_styleguides/ to the project root at conductor/code_styleguides/." and "You MUST ONLY propose and copy guides from assets/code_styleguides/." The style guides are rules for the agent, that is, configuration.

The state of a track: "Create metadata.json with the track ID, type, status". Versions 0.1.0 to 0.3.1 recorded the progress of the setup (https://github.com/gemini-cli-extensions/conductor/blob/conductor-v0.3.1/commands/conductor/setup.toml): "Read State File: Check for the existence of conductor/setup_state.json." and "Immediately after creating the conductor directory, you MUST create conductor/setup_state.json". setup_state.json anchors the rows of Conductor.

The setup command copies style guides that the agent follows: "Generate selected style guides from `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/templates/code_styleguides/`", and the plugin's README calls them "Language-specific conventions" (https://github.com/wshobson/agents/blob/main/plugins/conductor/README.md). The style guides are rules for the agent, that is, configuration.

The state of a track: "Create `metadata.json`:", with the track's status and the counts of its completed phases and tasks. The setup command records its progress: "Load or create `conductor/setup_state.json`:" and "Update `setup_state.json` after each successful step" (https://github.com/wshobson/agents/blob/main/plugins/conductor/commands/setup.md).

"Setup installs the shared runtime and module scripts under _bmad/." Version 4 installs into .bmad-core/ ("The `.bmad-core/core-config.yaml` file is a critical config", https://github.com/bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD/blob/V4/docs/user-guide.md) and its expansion packs into folders of their own: "let expansionDotFolder = path.join(installDir, `.${packId}`);" (https://github.com/bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD/blob/V4/tools/installer/lib/installer.js). The alpha releases of version 6 installed into "├── bmad/ # Centralized installation" (https://github.com/bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD/blob/v6.0.0-alpha.7/docs/installers-bundlers/installers-modules-platforms-reference.md) and, from alpha.8, into .bmad/: "What is the root folder for BMAD installation? (Recommended: .bmad)" (https://github.com/bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD/blob/v6.0.0-alpha.15/src/core/module.yaml). These folders anchor the document rows.
Party mode is a discussion among the agents. It writes "the optional end-of-session keepsake", a "self-contained HTML" document, and a memory of the room: "It is memory, not a transcript."

The standards are configuration: "agent-os/standards/ Your coding standards, organized by domain." Version 1 installed its instructions and standards into the project (https://github.com/buildermethods/agent-os/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): "It no longer references instructions or standards that reside elsewhere on your system. These all get installed directly into your project's .agent-os folder". Version 2 installed its commands into agent-os/commands/ (https://buildermethods.com/agent-os/v2/write-spec: "Check your agent-os/commands/write-spec/"), version 2.0 its roles ("where your roles/implementers.yml and roles/verifiers.yml contained convoluted lists of agents that could be assigned to implement tasks"), and version 2 its configuration (https://github.com/buildermethods/agent-os/blob/v2.1.1/scripts/project-update.sh installs "- agent-os/config.yml"). agent-os/standards/ and agent-os/config.yml anchor the document rows.

Configuration and state of Task Master. The migration guide: "config.json # Configuration (was .taskmasterconfig)" and "templates/ # Example/template files". The command reference (https://github.com/eyaltoledano/claude-task-master/blob/main/docs/command-reference.md): "State is stored in .taskmaster/state.json in your project root. It maintains important information like the current tag." .taskmaster/CLAUDE.md holds the instructions for Claude Code (https://github.com/eyaltoledano/claude-task-master/blob/1c7365cab1f1d8ee5b0ecc2292a9ba9cf5efea2e/src/profiles/claude.js): "Copy Task Master instructions to .taskmaster/CLAUDE.md".

The README of version 1 says "Install this repository into your project", and the repository's ccpm/ folder holds placeholders: ccpm/prds/.gitkeep, ccpm/epics/.gitkeep and the README of ccpm/context/, which says "When fully initialized, this directory contains:". The commands write into .claude/: "Output: .claude/prds/feature-name.md" and "Output: .claude/epics/feature-name/epic.md".

The compound skill keeps what a team learned: "Capture the learning into `docs/solutions/`", one document for each solved problem with the front matter module, tags and problem_type. These are notes on past work, not plans of work to do.

The skills read their settings there: "Read `docs_root` from `<repo-root>/.compound-engineering/config.yaml` only". A docs_root moves the plans and requirements to another folder, which the rows do not read.
"Put reports, analyses, summaries in `claudedocs/` directory"; only workflow_* and research_* files have rows.
"Put reports, analyses, summaries in `geminidocs/` directory"; only research_* files have a row.

"Edit templates and rules in `{{KIRO_DIR}}/settings/` to match your team's workflow.", with "`templates/`: document structure for requirements, design, tasks." and "`rules/`: AI generation principles and judgment criteria." The templates anchor cc-sdd's steering row.
The metadata of a mission: "Feature metadata and mission" and "Machine-readable WP manifest with `plan_concern_refs` traceability to IC-## entries".
"Each run is recorded in `codev/maintain/`": the record of a maintenance run, which audits and removes unused code, rather than a plan.

"Create your own templates in `.spec-workflow/templates/`". The workspace initializer copies the default templates there and writes a README into user-templates/: "This directory allows you to create custom templates that override the default Spec Workflow templates." (https://github.com/Pimzino/spec-workflow-mcp/blob/d38e82eaa8a6a2f5480285fa1feb8cf8378c86e0/src/core/workspace-initializer.ts).
The setup writes .claude/ with "templates/ # Document templates" beside the specs and the steering documents.

layout: .kittify/templates/, .kittify/missions/, .kittify/config.yaml, the files of .kittify/charter/ other than charter.md
notes: .kittify/ "Contains Spec Kitty configuration, templates, and project memory.", with "templates/ # Document templates" and "missions/ # Mission configurations". The charter has a row of its own, and the files derived from it are configuration: "Extracted Config | `governance.yaml`, `directives.yaml`, `metadata.yaml` | Auto-generated (never edit)" (https://github.com/spec-kitty/spec-kitty/blob/main/docs/changelog/2x/doctrine-and-charter.md).
"templates/ # Customizable templates", with "spec.md # Specification template", "plan.md # Planning template" and "task.md # Task template".

"`.autospec/config.yml` | Local project configuration", init "Creates `.autospec/init.yml` to track initialization settings" and "Creates `.autospec/.gitignore` for local runtime files", and a profile overlay is loaded from "`.autospec/profiles/<name>.yml`". The constitution in .autospec/ is a planning document and has a row.
"Configure in `.codev/config.json` (created by `codev init` or `codev adopt`)". Codev's documents are in codev/ and have rows.

The setup "Generates `.metaswarm/project-profile.json` with your configuration", and "Configuration: `.metaswarm/external-tools.yaml`." (https://github.com/dsifry/metaswarm/blob/main/USAGE.md). The models of the phases: "edit `.metaswarm/models.yaml`, then run `/update`" (https://github.com/dsifry/metaswarm/blob/main/README.md).
"LeanSpec configuration is stored in `.lean-spec/config.json` in your project root." and "Template files must exist in `.lean-spec/templates/`". The configuration file anchors LeanSpec's spec rows.

The installer "also adds `.ab-method/` (workflow definitions and the path index)", and "A project's own `.ab-method/structure/index.yaml` overrides the bundled one." The folder anchors AB Method's document rows. A plugin install keeps no such folder, "Nothing is copied into your project; the plugin updates on its own.", and the rows then count no document of the project.

The engine and the rules that agents follow. Version 2 "projects the selected engine into your harness's own directory ... `.aidlc/` on opencode and GitHub Copilot". Version 1 copied its rules: "`aws-aidlc-rule-details/` — detailed rules conditionally referenced by the core rules", "cp -R ~/Downloads/aidlc-rules/aws-aidlc-rule-details/* .aidlc-rule-details/" and "cp -R ~/Downloads/aidlc-rules/aws-aidlc-rule-details .kiro/" (https://github.com/awslabs/aidlc-workflows/blob/v1.0.0/README.md).

A space's method: "memory/ THE METHOD — how this team works (committed)", with the framework defaults, the team's and the project's practices, "phases/ phase-scoped rules" and its templates of the documents.

What a team gives the agents of a space to read: "knowledge/ DOMAIN KNOWLEDGE — standards an agent reads (committed)", with "documents/ YOUR ORIGINALS — PDFs, Word, Markdown (you own this)" and the catalog that the tool derives from them. These are the team's own standards, not documents of a piece of work.

layout: PROMPT.md, fix_plan.md, @fix_plan.md, AGENT.md, specs/ at the root (ghuntley); IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md with PROMPT_plan.md (ralph-playbook); .ralph/PROMPT.md, .ralph/AGENT.md; .claude/ralph-loop.local.md; .gemini/ralph/state.json
notes: "while :; do cat PROMPT.md | claude-code ; done", "create/update a fix_plan.md": bare root names. frankbria's PROMPT.md and AGENT.md are instructions; the Anthropic ralph-loop plugin and the Gemini CLI Ralph extension keep loop state only.
The stdlib folder holds conventions rather than specs: "Team conventions: Add specs/stdlib/convention-name.md for reusable patterns".

Ralph Orchestrator supports "Claude Code, Kiro, Gemini CLI, Codex" and more. Archcore's reference documents and records: "A doc is non-behavioral reference material", a guide gives "Step-by-step instructions for completing a specific task.", an evidence is "A record of one external material: a report, a page, a dataset, an interview.", a task type is "A proven workflow for a recurring implementation task." and a cpat "Records how and why a coding convention or pattern changed." Its specs, plans, architecture decision records and the requirement, proposal and investigation types count. The plan command writes a runbook as a guide, "| runbook | `guide` |" (https://github.com/archcore-ai/archcore/blob/5a67523420a3c81d7282b5991be6ffef3254167d/plugins/archcore/skills/_shared/delta-routing.md), and "A data migration that people run by hand adds a migration runbook." (https://github.com/archcore-ai/archcore/blob/main/README.md). Such a runbook gives the steps of an operation, as any other guide does, and its type does not tell it from a how-to.

An archived document moves "to the same relative path under `backlog/archive/docs/`". Its tasks, drafts, decisions and milestones count.

"It also records the agent id in `spec/fspec-config.json` (existing keys are preserved)." The agent documentation that init writes under spec/ is "the full fspec workflow guide (work unit management, ACDD phases, Gherkin conventions, CLI command reference) tailored to that agent".

The installed skill keeps "Templates, scripts, reference docs", and "Templates and scripts are relative to this installed `SKILL.md`." The agent starts a plan from them: "Copy these templates to start". The rows leave out every path below a templates/ folder.
`scripts/set-active-plan.sh` writes the pointer: "Switch or inspect the active plan pointer (`.planning/.active_plan`)." It names the selected plan folder and is no document.

They record a session that questions a decision, a session that explains code, the stages of building a prompt or a skill, and the sources of a response to a proposal request. hve-core 1.1.0 (https://github.com/microsoft/hve-core/blob/hve-core-v1.1.0/.github/agents/task-planner.agent.md) writes "`.copilot-tracking/prompts/` - Implementation prompts (`implement-task-description.prompt.md`)" and deletes the prompt once the plan is implemented: "Delete .copilot-tracking/prompts/{{implement_task_description}}.prompt.md".

"Write the completed description to `thoughts/shared/prs/{number}_description.md`" (https://github.com/humanlayer/humanlayer/blob/99abe673498cf8bdcd5f989aebe9406a27185b3b/.claude/commands/describe_pr.md): a pull request description. The ralph commands "use `linear` cli to fetch the selected item into thoughts with the ticket number - ./thoughts/shared/tickets/ENG-xxxx.md" (https://github.com/humanlayer/humanlayer/blob/99abe673498cf8bdcd5f989aebe9406a27185b3b/.claude/commands/ralph_plan.md), a copy of an issue of the tracker, as HumanLayer's Linear CLI writes it: "`linear get-issue ENG-XXXX > thoughts/shared/tickets/eng-XXXX.md`" (https://github.com/humanlayer/humanlayer/blob/main/apps/linear-cli/README.md). No live page describes the commands, so the row cites the describe-pr skill that replaced describe_pr and quotes the files of commit 99abe673, the last with the commands.

The configure-workspaces skill writes the configuration of the worktrees of a task: "The workspace config files control how worktrees are created", with .humanlayer/workspace.json as "shared team configuration, safe to commit" and .humanlayer/workspace.local.json with "machine-specific overrides, gitignored".

The folder of a task holds "pr-description.md", the "PR description | Review summary, changes, and validation", which describe-pr writes and makes the body of the pull request: "Use `.humanlayer/tasks/{task-slug}/pr-description.md` when the task directory exists; otherwise use `.humanlayer/tasks/pr-{number}/description.md`." (https://github.com/humanlayer/humanlayer/blob/main/apps/riptide-rpi-claude-plugin/skills/describe-pr/SKILL.md). A large pull request adds "pr-walkthrough.html". "Oneshot starts implementation from `ticket.md`.", the issue that a task starts from: "The resulting `ticket.md` includes the issue details, comments, and source link." (https://github.com/humanlayer/humanlayer/blob/main/apps/docs/guide/github-integration.md). A pull request description and a copy of an issue of the tracker, as for thoughts/shared/prs/ and thoughts/shared/tickets/.

The folder of a task keeps HTML pages beside the PRD and the TDD: "mockup-<description>.html # optional PRD support" and "diagram-<description>.html # optional TDD support". The create-prd skill (https://github.com/humanlayer/humanlayer/blob/main/apps/riptide-rpi-claude-plugin/skills/create-prd/SKILL.md): "Write HTML files to `.humanlayer/tasks/{task-slug}/mockup-{description}.html`". Mockups and diagrams are no planning documents, as for the mockups and pages of QualityLayer.
"`.specs/scratchpad/` | Temporary working files (gitignored)", "`.specs/analysis/` | Codebase impact analysis files (gitignored)" and "`.specs/reports/` | Generated reports (gitignored)".

sddw writes reports after the work: "a completion report (`task-N-<slug>.done.md`) is written to `implement/tasks/`", the verification "report.md # FR-by-FR pass/fail, test results, deviations, warnings" and the self-improvement "report.md # findings, proposals, applied/skipped changes". Its requirements, design, task files and code analysis count.

GAAI's stories, epics, plans, PRDs and approach evaluations count.

The state of specs.md's flows: "state.yaml # Central state tracking" of FIRE, "session.yaml # Session state (resumable)" of Ideation, the "Run Log: .specs-fire/runs/{run-id}/run.md" of a FIRE run (https://github.com/fabriqaai/specs.md/blob/main/src/flows/fire/agents/builder/skills/run-execute/SKILL.md), and the "construction-log entries" and "inception-log entries" of AI-DLC (https://github.com/fabriqaai/specs.md/blob/main/src/flows/aidlc/memory-bank.yaml).

Its specs, plans, task lists, checklists, research, sprint plans and contracts count.

autospec analyze writes a report: "Perform cross-artifact consistency analysis", with the type "`analysis` - Cross-artifact analysis (analysis.yaml)". Its spec, plan, tasks, checklists and constitution count.

The AI-DLC flow keeps its coding conventions beside the other project standards: "standards/ # Project standards ... tech-stack.md ... coding-standards.md ... system-architecture.md". As FIRE's .specs-fire/standards/coding-standards.md, they are conventions that the agents follow. Its tech stack and system architecture count.

The reports of a bolt of the AI-DLC flow: "`implementation-walkthrough.md` - `memory-bank/bolts/{bolt-id}/implementation-walkthrough.md`", "Location: `memory-bank/bolts/{bolt-id}/test-walkthrough.md`" and, in a DDD bolt, "Default: `memory-bank/bolts/{bolt-id}/ddd-03-test-report.md`" (https://github.com/fabriqaai/specs.md/blob/main/src/flows/aidlc/templates/construction/bolt-types/ddd-construction-bolt.md). They record what a bolt changed and tested, as FIRE's walkthroughs and test reports do. The plan and the designs of a bolt count.

The plan agent of OpenCode 2 writes its plans outside the repository, since the permissions page gives it the policy "Allows questions; denies edits except files under ~/.opencode/plan". OpenCode 1 writes them into .opencode/plans/ at the worktree root of a git repository, which planning_document_patterns.csv counts.

Beside its seven documents, a task folder holds `artifacts/`, the local files that a task makes with their revisions, "`records/` | The raw output of every command, and `pull-request-body.md`" and "`evidence/` | Pictures and recordings the checks made". The files that a task keeps for the project go into `.qualitylayer/artifacts/<name>/`, "committed with the change (older `.qualitylayer/designs/` still read)", and the files kept only on the person's computer into `docs/artifacts/`, "out of git". Such a folder holds "a mockup, diagram or clickable set of pages you work on with your agent" (https://github.com/maxritter/qualitylayer/blob/main/docs/docusaurus/docs/artifacts.md). Mockups, pages, command output and pictures are no planning documents.

A task folder keeps "`reviews/` | The Plan review and second opinion, when they ran". The page names no file of the folder, and whether a review of the Plan counts, as the REVIEWS.md of a Get Shit Done phase does, is open until a repository shows the files.

Project memory that a person shares through Git: "Eligible lessons are written to `.qualitylayer/memories/` with a readable `LESSONS.md`." and "Review, commit and push them yourself." Lessons of earlier tasks, as the .specweave/memory/ of SpecWeave, not the documents of a task.

Pilot Shell's project memory, which QualityLayer imports: a person selects the project, "then choose its JSONL or Markdown files from `.pilot/memories/` in that repository." Lessons, not the plans of a task.

Version 4.0 adds a folder to a task: "prototype/ # DISPOSABLE. prototype-ui's self-contained HTML picker for a task adding new UI.", and "the folder is deleted when the task completes. Gitignored." The pick goes into the progress tracker: "Writes the picked variant into the tracker's `## UI Spec`."

A quick task's code review, "Output: ${QUICK_DIR}/${quick_id}-REVIEW.md", and its deferred items, "If `${QUICK_DIR}/${quick_id}-deferred-items.md` exists". As for the REVIEW.md and deferred-items.md of a phase, whether a code review or a list of deferred work is a planning document is open, and the quick task row counts the plan, summary, context, research and verification.
The project's settings, such as the optional skills, which "install when `skills.enabled` in `.specweave/config.json` lists them".

The CLI's own files: "purge stale `.specweave/state` files (dry run by default)", "recent hook warnings, errors and blocks from `.specweave/logs/hooks.jsonl`", "Backups land in `.specweave/backups/`." and, since 3.1.3, the cards of a branch without an increment, "writes `C-NN` cards to `.specweave/cards/<branch>.jsonl`". JSON lines and logs that the CLI writes, not documents.

The index of every active increment that a handoff of all of them writes: "It writes `.specweave/handoffs/<date>-INDEX.md` and `index.json` with one row per active increment: tasks done, open acceptance criteria, last activity, what it waits on, and a resume prompt to paste into a new thread." It records the state of the increments, whose spec, tasks, plan and handoff count.

The engine that version 2 installs for Claude Code: "installed projects use the same relative paths under `.claude/`", among them the checks, "Sensor manifests live at: dist/claude/.claude/sensors/aidlc-<id>.md", the stage definitions, such as "dist/claude/.claude/aidlc-common/stages/construction/ci-pipeline.md", and a project's own sensor, "a new project-tier manifest at `<project>/.claude/sensors/aidlc-<id>.md`".

The index of the stories of AI-DLC, which the inception agent updates as it writes each story, "After creating EACH story, IMMEDIATELY update the index.", at "Path: `memory-bank/story-index.md`" or "Path: `memory-bank/intents/{intent-name}/story-index.md`". It records the status of each story, such as "No marker = Planned (not yet created)", and the stories count.

The construction agent lists every architecture decision record of the bolts there, "For each ADR created, add an entry to `memory-bank/standards/decision-index.md`:" (https://github.com/fabriqaai/specs.md/blob/main/src/flows/aidlc/templates/construction/bolt-types/ddd-construction-bolt.md), and "This index tracks all Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) created during Construction bolts." It is a lookup for the agents, "Use this to find relevant prior decisions when working on related features.", and the records count in their bolts.

The operations agent keeps the "Operations Context (Deployment, Monitoring)" in memory-bank/operations/, and its deploy skill records each deployment in the folder of the unit, "Append to `deployment/history.md`:" and "`{unit-path}/deployment/history.md`" (https://github.com/fabriqaai/specs.md/blob/main/src/flows/aidlc/skills/operations/deploy.md). They record what was built and deployed, and the documents of the unit count.
